submitter: bugs_open/440 lane, phase 2 part 2 — the raw-SQL producer door. Part 1 (the Go producers, one shared helper) was APPROVED r1 on correlation c7dab2c1, with its two substantive advisories actioned in code. This round closes the door no Go guard can reach: hand-written migrations that mint page_rerender items. scripts/pattern-check.py is IN council scope by the owner ruling of 2026-08-24, which is why this is here.
rationale: RFC_062 phase 3 narrows the page-rerender gate to spec.routing_reason. Every item minted with spec.reason alone will then route to ASSEMBLE — stored HTML re-shipped, work item complete, page untouched, nothing saying so — which is bugs_open/440 itself. The Go producers are converted (phase 2 part 1). Raw-SQL migrations are the remaining producer class, and they bypass every compiler and every Go guard: `[MEASURED 2026-09-03]` migrations 696, 693 and 701 minted page_rerender items this week. THE DESIGN PROBLEM THIS SUBMISSION IS ABOUT is not detecting the shape — it is that a Python checker needs the vocabulary, and hardcoding it would create a THIRD copy of a list whose second copy is the reason bugs_open/404 exists (the live gate knew five values, Go knew three, for eight days, because two lanes appended one each on the same day and neither touched Go). So the check READS the vocabulary from the Go constants at run time and, when it cannot, reports that LOUDLY and checks nothing — because a vocabulary check running on an empty vocabulary passes every file and reads exactly like a clean bill of health. Both failure modes are proven by mutation, not asserted. The second half is the authoring door proper: a LANDMINES entry, which is this estate's system of record for 'what will mislead you when you TOUCH this thing' and reaches an author BEFORE they have a symptom — including the two unapplied _HOLD migrations already in the bad state.

plan.summary: One advisory check in scripts/pattern-check.py that derives the reason vocabulary from platform/livespec/rerender_reasons.go (never a copy), fires on a TOUCHED migration minting page_rerender with an in-vocabulary reason and no routing_reason, or with a routing-shaped value nobody declared, and refuses to run blind if the vocabulary cannot be read; plus a LANDMINES entry carrying the rule, the check, the measured noise figure, and the two unapplied _HOLD files already affected.

edits.rationale: Advisory, fires only on migration files a commit touches, using the existing MIGRATION_DIR + migration_is_lintable + strip_comments idiom of check_unguarded_migration_insert. The vocabulary is derived from the Go constants; an unreadable or reshaped source produces a finding that says so instead of a silent pass. Free prose is deliberately NOT flagged (owner ruling D4: the annotation stays free forever), and a non-page_rerender item type is ignored.

edits.symbol: entry: a migration that mints a page_rerender item must stamp routing_reason
edits.rationale: The authoring door. LANDMINES is the estate's system of record for prospective traps (owner ruling D10) and is synced into doc_notes so agents read it too — the right vehicle rather than a new conventions doc nobody opens. The entry carries the rule, the why-it-looks-right, the exact jsonb_build_object form, the check's existence AND its stated blind spot (it only sees touched files), and the two unapplied _HOLD migrations already in the bad state.
edits.sketch:
- **the check — stamp BOTH, with the same value:**
  ```sql
  jsonb_build_object('reason', 'template_changed', 'routing_reason', 'template_changed', ...)
  ```
- **⚠ TWO UNAPPLIED `_HOLD` FILES ARE ALREADY IN THIS STATE** `[MEASURED 2026-09-03]`: `683_content_listing_rerender_after_roll_HOLD.sql` and `701_retype_357_population_by_adoption_HOLD.sql` carry `reason` with no routing key and no `-- APPLIED` line.

grounded_in: Why the vocabulary must not be copied — bugs_open/404's own record [platform/livespec/rerender_reasons.go header]: 'On 2026-08-18 two lanes appended a value each to the live gate — template_changed (migration 460) and literal_markdown (473) — and neither touched Go. So the gate knew five and the Go reader knew three.' A hardcoded list in pattern-check.py would be the third copy.

The check derives it, verified by execution [2026-09-03]: _rerender_vocabulary(None) returns exactly ['cta_links_stale','image_landed','literal_markdown','section_data_resolved','template_changed'] — identical to livespec's constants, read from the file rather than typed.

Both blind-failure modes proven by mutation, not asserted [2026-09-03]: pointing VOCAB_SOURCE at a nonexistent file → 1 finding, 'the reason vocabulary could not be read — … is empty or missing'; pointing it at a real Go file with no Reason* constants → 1 finding, 'no Reason* constants found … the declaration shape changed'. Neither mutation produces a silent pass.

Behaviour proven across five fixtures [2026-09-03]: page_rerender + in-vocabulary reason, no routing key → FIRES; same with routing_reason present → silent; routing-SHAPED unknown ('tool_retirement') → FIRES with the did-you-mean message; free prose ('FCA rule citation corrected by migration 696') → SILENT (owner ruling D4); item_type 'needs_page' with an in-vocabulary reason → SILENT.

Noise measured before shipping [2026-09-03]: run over the whole corpus, 844 lintable migrations produce 11 findings — and the check only sees files a commit touches, so the practical rate is lower. Two of the 11 are unapplied _HOLD files (683, 701; `grep -c '^-- APPLIED'` returns 0 for both), which is a live finding rather than corpus noise: applied after phase 3 they mint items that assemble.
plan.risks: (1) The classifier is textual: it reads a migration's SQL for 'page_rerender' and JSON-ish reason keys, so a migration that builds its spec in an exotic way (string concatenation across lines, a PL/pgSQL variable) can pass unflagged. Advisory-only, so a miss costs nothing that phase 3's census will not catch; over-firing is the failure mode that would matter and the corpus census bounds it at 11/844. (2) It reads Go source with a regex, so a change to how the constants are declared silently reduces coverage — which is exactly why the no-constants case is a LOUD finding rather than an empty set, and why that path is mutation-proved. (3) It cannot see a migration written before it existed until someone touches that file; stated in the entry rather than left implicit, and phase 3's census is the backstop. (4) LANDMINES is append-only and shared; the entry was appended and the sync run (`landmines-verify-dispatch.sh`), which is the estate's required order. (5) This completes phase 2 but NOT the bug: phase 3 (the gate flip, the review-routing refusal per owner ruling D1, and the CHECK constraint per D3, co-signed with the 404 lane per D2) remains, blocked on confirming the conditional evaluator's missing-key-vs-empty-string behaviour.
